title: Bonding in Coordination Compounds (VBT, CFT, CFSE, Magnetic Properties, & Color)
syllabus: Valence Bond Theory (VBT) applied to coordination complexes: Inner orbital (d2sp3, dsp2) and outer orbital (sp3d2, sp3) complexes, orbital hybridization schemes, limitations of VBT; Crystal Field Theory (CFT): Crystal field splitting in octahedral (Δo) and tetrahedral (Δt) environments, relationship between Δo and Δt (Δt = 4/9 Δo); Spectrochemical series and ligand field strength; Pairing energy (P), high-spin vs low-spin complexes for d4 to d7 configurations; Crystal Field Stabilization Energy (CFSE) calculation for octahedral and tetrahedral complexes; Magnetic properties (spin-only magnetic moment formula μ = √[n(n+2)] BM); Color of coordination complexes, d-d transitions, Laporte and spin selection rules, complementary colors, Jahn-Teller distortion (qualitative), and synergic bonding in metal carbonyls

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] The crystal field stabilization energy (CFSE, ignoring pairing energy) for a high-spin $d^6$ octahedral complex is:
questions.solution:
In an octahedral crystal field, the $d$-orbitals split into a lower triply degenerate $t_{2g}$ set (stabilized by $-0.4\ \Delta_o$ per electron) and a higher doubly degenerate $e_g$ set (destabilized by $+0.6\ \Delta_o$ per electron).
For a high-spin $d^6$ configuration (where $\Delta_o < P$):
Electrons fill according to Hund's rule: $t_{2g}^4 e_g^2$.
$$\text{CFSE} = [n(t_{2g}) \times (-0.4) + n(e_g) \times (+0.6)]\ \Delta_o$$
$$\text{CFSE} = [4 \times (-0.4) + 2 \times (+0.6)]\ \Delta_o = [-1.6 + 1.2]\ \Delta_o = -0.4\ \Delta_o$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] The hybridization and magnetic behavior of the complex $[\text{Ni}(\text{CN})_4]^{2-}$ are respectively:
questions.solution:
1. Oxidation state of nickel in $[\text{Ni}(\text{CN})_4]^{2-}$:
$$x + 4(-1) = -2 \implies x = +2$$
$$\text{Ni}^{2+}: [\text{Ar}] 3d^8 4s^0 4p^0$$
2. Cyanide ($\text{CN}^-$) is a strong field carbon-donor ligand that induces pairing of the two unpaired electrons in the $3d$ subshell:
$$3d^8 \rightarrow 4\text{ pairs in four } 3d \text{ orbitals}$$
3. This leaves one inner $3d$ orbital vacant. The metal uses one $3d$, one $4s$, and two $4p$ orbitals to form four $dsp^2$ hybrid orbitals (square planar geometry).
4. Because all electrons are paired ($n = 0$), the complex is diamagnetic.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] The correct order of ligand field strength in the spectrochemical series is:
questions.solution:
The spectrochemical series is an experimentally determined sequence that ranks ligands based on the magnitude of crystal field splitting ($\Delta_o$) they induce:
Halide donors $< \text{Oxygen donors} < \text{Nitrogen donors} < \text{Carbon donors}$
$$\text{I}^- < \text{Br}^- < \text{S}^{2-} < \text{SCN}^- < \text{Cl}^- < \text{F}^- < \text{OH}^- < \text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-} < \text{H}_2\text{O} < \text{NCS}^- < \text{edta}^{4-} < \text{NH}_3 < \text{en} < \text{CN}^- < \text{CO}$$
Option A matches the correct sequence.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] Which of the following complex ions absorbs light of the SHORTEST wavelength in the visible region?
questions.solution:
The excitation of electrons during $d-d$ transitions absorbs light energy corresponding to the crystal field splitting energy:
$$\Delta_o = h\nu = \frac{hc}{\lambda} \implies \lambda \propto \frac{1}{\Delta_o}$$
1. A higher crystal field splitting ($\Delta_o$) requires higher energy, which corresponds to a shorter wavelength ($\lambda$) of absorbed light.
2. Among the coordinated ligands, cyanide ($\text{CN}^-$) is the strongest field ligand in the spectrochemical series, producing the largest $\Delta_o$.
3. Order of $\Delta_o$: $[\text{Co}(\text{CN})_6]^{3-} > [\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6]^{3+} > [\text{Co}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+} > [\text{CoF}_6]^{3-}$.
Consequently, $[\text{Co}(\text{CN})_6]^{3-}$ absorbs light with the highest energy and shortest wavelength (absorbing in the ultraviolet/violet region).

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] The relation between the crystal field splitting energy in a tetrahedral complex ($\Delta_t$) and an octahedral complex ($\Delta_o$) for the same metal ion and ligands is:
questions.solution:
In a tetrahedral coordination complex:
1. There are only $4$ ligands instead of $6$ in an octahedral complex, reducing electrostatic repulsion by a factor of $\frac{4}{6} = \frac{2}{3}$.
2. The ligands in a tetrahedral geometry do not point directly at any of the metal $d$-orbitals (they approach between the Cartesian axes), which reduces the splitting efficiency by another factor of $\frac{2}{3}$.
Combining both geometric effects gives:
$$\Delta_t = \frac{2}{3} \times \frac{2}{3}\ \Delta_o = \frac{4}{9}\ \Delta_o$$
Because $\Delta_t$ is roughly half of $\Delta_o$, it rarely exceeds the electron pairing energy ($P$). Consequently, tetrahedral complexes are almost exclusively high-spin.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] The spin-only magnetic moments of $[\text{Fe}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$ and $[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]^{4-}$ are respectively:
questions.solution:
Both complexes contain $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ with electronic configuration $[\text{Ar}] 3d^6$:
1. In $[\text{Fe}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$, water is a weak field ligand ($\Delta_o < P$), forming a high-spin complex:
$$t_{2g}^4 e_g^2 \implies n = 4\text{ unpaired electrons}$$
$$\mu_s = \sqrt{4(4 + 2)} = \sqrt{24} \approx 4.899\text{ BM} \approx 4.90\text{ BM}$$
2. In $[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]^{4-}$, cyanide is a strong field ligand ($\Delta_o > P$), forming a low-spin complex:
$$t_{2g}^6 e_g^0 \implies n = 0\text{ unpaired electrons}$$
$$\mu_s = 0\text{ BM} \quad (\text{diamagnetic})$$
Therefore, the magnetic moments are $4.90\text{ BM}$ and $0\text{ BM}$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] Synergic bonding in metal carbonyls, such as $[\text{Ni}(\text{CO})_4]$, involves:
options: $\sigma$-donation of a lone pair from $\text{CO}$ to a vacant metal $d$-orbital and $\pi$-back-donation from a filled metal $d$-orbital into the empty $\pi^*$ antibonding orbital of $\text{CO}$
$\sigma$-donation from metal to $\text{CO}$ and $\pi$-donation from $\text{CO}$ to metal
Pure electrostatic attraction between $\text{Ni}^{2+}$ and polarized carbonyl dipoles
$\pi$-overlap between filled $s$-orbitals of metal and vacant $p$-orbitals of carbon
questions.solution:
Synergic (cooperative) bonding in transition metal carbonyls consists of two complementary components:
1. **$\text{M} \leftarrow \text{C}$ $\sigma$-bond:** Donation of the lone pair of electrons on the carbon atom of $\text{CO}$ into an empty hybrid orbital of the transition metal.
2. **$\text{M} \rightarrow \text{C}$ $\pi$-back-bonding:** Back-donation of electron density from a filled non-bonding $d$-orbital of the metal into the vacant $\pi^*$ antibonding molecular orbital of $\text{CO}$.
This back-donation strengthens the $\text{M}-\text{C}$ bond while simultaneously weakening the $\text{C}\equiv\text{O}$ bond (lengthening the $\text{C}-\text{O}$ bond and decreasing its IR stretching frequency).

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] Which of the following electronic configurations in an octahedral complex will show a significant Jahn-Teller distortion?
questions.solution:
The Jahn-Teller theorem states that any non-linear molecular system in a degenerate electronic state is unstable and will undergo geometric distortion to lower its symmetry and lift the degeneracy.
1. A significant (strong) Jahn-Teller distortion occurs when the higher-energy $e_g$ orbitals (which point directly at the incoming ligands) are **asymmetrically occupied**.
2. Configurations with asymmetrically occupied $e_g$ orbitals include:
- High-spin $d^4$ ($t_{2g}^3 e_g^1$)
- Low-spin $d^7$ ($t_{2g}^6 e_g^1$)
- $d^9$ ($t_{2g}^6 e_g^3$, e.g., $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ complexes)
3. Symmetrically filled subshells (like $t_{2g}^3 e_g^0, t_{2g}^6 e_g^0,$ and $t_{2g}^3 e_g^2$) experience no electronic degeneracy in $e_g$ and do not exhibit Jahn-Teller distortion.
Hence, high-spin $d^4$ shows a pronounced Jahn-Teller distortion.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] An aqueous solution of $[\text{Ti}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+}$ exhibits a purple-violet color. When the solution is heated to drive off coordinated water, the anhydrous substance becomes colorless because:
options: In the absence of ligands, crystal field splitting does not occur, making $d-d$ transitions impossible
Titanium is reduced to metallic titanium
The complex changes to a tetrahedral geometry with zero crystal field splitting
questions.solution:
1. In $[\text{Ti}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+}$, titanium is in the $+3$ oxidation state ($3d^1$).
2. The six coordinated water ligands create an octahedral crystal field that splits the five degenerate $3d$ orbitals into $t_{2g}$ and $e_g$ sets.
3. Absorption of visible light (yellow-green region, $\approx 500\text{ nm}$) promotes the single $d$-electron from $t_{2g}$ to $e_g$ ($t_{2g}^1 e_g^0 \rightarrow t_{2g}^0 e_g^1$). The transmitted complementary light is purple-violet.
4. When the ligands are removed upon heating, the crystal field vanishes and the five $3d$ orbitals become completely degenerate again. Without energy splitting, $d-d$ transitions cannot take place, and the anhydrous substance appears colorless.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] The crystal field stabilization energy (CFSE) of a low-spin $d^5$ octahedral complex (ignoring pairing energy) is:
questions.solution:
For a low-spin $d^5$ configuration in an octahedral field, strong field ligands cause $\Delta_o > P$.
All five electrons pair up in the lower $t_{2g}$ orbitals:
$$\text{Configuration} = t_{2g}^5 e_g^0$$
Calculate the CFSE:
$$\text{CFSE} = [5 \times (-0.4\ \Delta_o) + 0 \times (+0.6\ \Delta_o)] = -2.0\ \Delta_o$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] Which of the following complex ions is an OUTER orbital octahedral complex?
questions.solution:
1. In $[\text{CoF}_6]^{3-}$, cobalt is in the $+3$ oxidation state ($3d^6$). Fluoride is a weak field ligand ($\Delta_o < P$), so it cannot force the pairing of $3d$ electrons. The four unpaired electrons remain in the inner $3d$ subshell ($t_{2g}^4 e_g^2$). Cobalt uses outer $4s, 4p,$ and $4d$ orbitals to form six $sp^3d^2$ hybrid orbitals. It is an **outer orbital (high-spin)** complex.
2. In $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$, $\text{NH}_3$ behaves as a strong field ligand with $\text{Co}^{3+}$, pairing all electrons ($t_{2g}^6 e_g^0$) to use inner $3d$ orbitals ($d^2sp^3$, inner orbital).
3. In $[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]^{3-}$, cyanide is a strong field ligand ($d^2sp^3$, inner orbital).
4. In $[\text{Cr}(\text{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$, $\text{Cr}^{3+}$ ($3d^3$) naturally has two empty $3d$ orbitals available for $d^2sp^3$ inner orbital hybridization.

questions.question: For a tetrahedral complex $[\text{FeCl}_4]^{2-}$, the electronic configuration and number of unpaired electrons under CFT are:
questions.solution:
1. Oxidation state of iron in $[\text{FeCl}_4]^{2-}$:
$$x + 4(-1) = -2 \implies x = +2$$
$$\text{Fe}^{2+}: [\text{Ar}] 3d^6$$
2. In a tetrahedral crystal field, the $d$-orbitals split into a lower doubly degenerate $e$ set and an upper triply degenerate $t_2$ set (inversion center is absent, so 'g' subscripts are omitted).
3. Since $\Delta_t$ is inherently small ($\Delta_t = \frac{4}{9}\Delta_o < P$), all tetrahedral complexes are high-spin.
4. Electrons fill as: $e^2 t_2^3 e^1 \implies e^3 t_2^3$.
5. The $e$ level contains one pair and one unpaired electron; the $t_2$ level contains three unpaired electrons.
$$\text{Total unpaired electrons} = 1 + 3 = 4$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] Which of the following compounds has the SHORTEST $\text{C}-\text{O}$ bond length?
questions.solution:
1. In metal carbonyls, $\pi$-back-donation from the metal into the $\pi^*$ orbital of $\text{CO}$ weakens the $\text{C}-\text{O}$ bond and increases its bond length relative to free carbon monoxide.
2. More negative charge on the metal complex increases electron density on the metal, enhancing back-donation into $\text{CO}$ and lengthening the $\text{C}-\text{O}$ bond: $[\text{V}(\text{CO})_6]^-$ has the longest $\text{C}-\text{O}$ bond.
3. In free, uncoordinated carbon monoxide ($\text{CO}$), there is no back-bonding from any metal center. The bond is an unperturbed triple bond ($112.8\text{ pm}$), which is shorter than the $\text{C}-\text{O}$ bond in any metal carbonyl complex.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] A complex $[\text{M}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$ has a spin-only magnetic moment of $3.87\text{ BM}$. The central transition metal ion $\text{M}^{2+}$ is:
questions.solution:
From the spin-only magnetic moment:
$$\mu_s = \sqrt{n(n + 2)} = 3.87\text{ BM} \implies n = 3\text{ unpaired electrons}$$
Water is a weak field ligand, so the complex is high-spin:
- $\text{Cr}^{2+}$ ($3d^4$): high-spin $t_{2g}^3 e_g^1 \implies n = 4$ ($\mu \approx 4.90\text{ BM}$)
- $\text{Mn}^{2+}$ ($3d^5$): high-spin $t_{2g}^3 e_g^2 \implies n = 5$ ($\mu \approx 5.92\text{ BM}$)
- $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ ($3d^6$): high-spin $t_{2g}^4 e_g^2 \implies n = 4$ ($\mu \approx 4.90\text{ BM}$)
- $\text{Co}^{2+}$ ($3d^7$): high-spin $t_{2g}^5 e_g^2 \implies n = 3$ ($\mu = \sqrt{3(5)} = \sqrt{15} \approx 3.87\text{ BM}$)
Therefore, the central metal ion is $\text{Co}^{2+}$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] Why is $[\text{Sc}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+}$ completely colorless, whereas $[\text{Cr}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+}$ is violet?
options: $\text{Sc}^{3+}$ has a $3d^0$ configuration with no $d$-electrons available for $d-d$ transitions
$\text{Sc}^{3+}$ undergoes intense charge transfer in the ultraviolet region
Water acts as a strong field ligand with scandium
questions.solution:
Color in coordination complexes typically arises from the absorption of visible light during $d-d$ transitions:
1. For $[\text{Sc}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+}$: Scandium is in the $+3$ oxidation state ($Z = 21$), with electronic configuration $[\text{Ar}] 3d^0$. With no $d$-electrons in the valence shell, $d-d$ transitions cannot occur, making the complex colorless.
2. For $[\text{Cr}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+}$: Chromium is in the $+3$ oxidation state with configuration $[\text{Ar}] 3d^3$. The three $d$-electrons occupy the $t_{2g}$ set ($t_{2g}^3 e_g^0$) and can undergo excitation into the empty $e_g$ orbitals upon absorbing yellow light, transmitting a violet color.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] The geometry and hybridization of the copper complex $[\text{Cu}(\text{NH}_3)_4]^{2+}$ according to Valence Bond Theory are:
questions.solution:
In $[\text{Cu}(\text{NH}_3)_4]^{2+}$:
- Copper is in the $+2$ oxidation state: $\text{Cu}^{2+} = [\text{Ar}] 3d^9$.
- X-ray crystallography confirms that $[\text{Cu}(\text{NH}_3)_4]^{2+}$ possesses a square planar geometry (due to Jahn-Teller effect on an octahedral precursor).
- In the classical Valence Bond Theory description, one electron from the $3d$ subshell is promoted to a higher $4p$ (or $4d$) orbital, freeing an inner $3d$ orbital to participate in $dsp^2$ hybridization (or alternatively, $sp^2d$ hybridization using the $4d_{x^2-y^2}$ orbital).
In standard JEE convention, it is classified as square planar with $dsp^2$ hybridization.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] In an octahedral crystal field, which of the following pairs of $d$-orbitals forms the higher-energy $e_g$ set?
questions.solution:
In an octahedral complex, the six ligands approach the central metal ion along the Cartesian coordinate axes ($\pm x, \pm y, \pm z$):
1. The $d_{x^2-y^2}$ and $d_{z^2}$ orbitals have lobes pointing directly along the $x, y,$ and $z$ axes.
2. Electrons in these orbitals experience greater electrostatic repulsion from the incoming negative ligands, raising them in energy by $+0.6\ \Delta_o$ above the barycenter.
3. This doubly degenerate axial set is designated as the $e_g$ set ($d_{x^2-y^2}, d_{z^2}$).
4. The $d_{xy}, d_{yz},$ and $d_{zx}$ orbitals point between the axes and form the lower-energy $t_{2g}$ set.

questions.question: Which of the following complexes is DIAMAGNETIC?
questions.solution:
Examine the electronic configurations of the complexes:
1. $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$: $\text{Co}^{3+}$ has configuration $3d^6$. Ammonia is a strong field ligand for $\text{Co}^{3+}$ ($\Delta_o > P$), causing complete electron pairing: $t_{2g}^6 e_g^0$. Because there are zero unpaired electrons ($n = 0$), the complex is diamagnetic.
2. $[\text{CoF}_6]^{3-}$: $\text{Co}^{3+}$ with weak field $\text{F}^-$, high-spin $t_{2g}^4 e_g^2 \implies n = 4$ (paramagnetic).
3. $[\text{FeF}_6]^{3-}$: $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ with weak field $\text{F}^-$, high-spin $t_{2g}^3 e_g^2 \implies n = 5$ (paramagnetic).
4. $[\text{Mn}(\text{CN})_6]^{3-}$: $\text{Mn}^{3+}$ ($3d^4$), low-spin $t_{2g}^4 e_g^0 \implies n = 2$ (paramagnetic).
Therefore, $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$ is diamagnetic.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] The crystal field splitting energy ($\Delta_o$) of a complex depends on which of the following factors?
options: Oxidation state of the metal, principal quantum number of $d$-orbitals ($3d < 4d < 5d$), and nature of the ligand
Oxidation state of the metal only
Only the mass of the central metal atom
questions.solution:
The magnitude of $\Delta_o$ depends on:
1. **Nature of the ligand:** Stronger field ligands (higher in the spectrochemical series) cause greater splitting.
2. **Oxidation state of the metal:** Higher positive charge on the metal draws ligands closer, increasing repulsion and splitting ($\Delta_o$ for $M^{3+} > M^{2+}$ by $\approx 50\%$).
3. **Principal quantum number ($3d < 4d < 5d$):** Moving from $3d$ to $4d$ to $5d$, orbitals extend further in space, interacting more strongly with ligands ($\Delta_o$ increases by $\approx 30-50\%$ down a triad; $4d$ and $5d$ complexes are almost always low-spin).
4. **Geometry of the complex:** $\Delta_t \approx \frac{4}{9}\Delta_o$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] When dimethylglyoxime ($\text{DMG}$) is added to an ammoniacal solution of nickel(II) chloride, a rosy-red precipitate of $[\text{Ni}(\text{dmg})_2]$ is formed. The geometry and magnetic nature of this complex are:
questions.solution:
In bis(dimethylglyoximato)nickel(II), $[\text{Ni}(\text{dmg})_2]$:
1. Nickel is in the $+2$ oxidation state: $\text{Ni}^{2+} = [\text{Ar}] 3d^8$.
2. Although $\text{DMG}$ coordinates through nitrogen atoms, chelation and intramolecular $\text{O}-\text{H}\cdots\text{O}$ hydrogen bonding stabilize a square planar framework.
3. The strong ligand field forces pairing of the two $3d$ electrons, giving a low-spin $3d^8$ configuration with one vacant inner $d$-orbital.
4. The complex uses $dsp^2$ hybridization, adopting a square planar geometry.
5. With zero unpaired electrons, it is diamagnetic.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] Calculate the crystal field stabilization energy (CFSE in units of $\Delta_o$, as an exact magnitude) for $[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]^{3-}$ in low-spin state, ignoring pairing energy.
questions.solution:
In $[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]^{3-}$:
- Iron is in the $+3$ oxidation state ($3d^5$).
- Cyanide is a strong field ligand, forming a low-spin complex:
$$t_{2g}^5 e_g^0$$
- Each $t_{2g}$ electron contributes $-0.4\ \Delta_o$:
$$\text{CFSE} = 5 \times (-0.4\ \Delta_o) = -2.0\ \Delta_o$$
The magnitude of the CFSE is $2.0$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] Find the number of unpaired electrons in the tetrahedral complex ion $[\text{NiCl}_4]^{2-}$.
questions.solution:
1. Oxidation state of nickel in $[\text{NiCl}_4]^{2-}$:
$$x + 4(-1) = -2 \implies x = +2$$
$$\text{Ni}^{2+}: [\text{Ar}] 3d^8$$
2. For tetrahedral geometry, chloride is a weak field ligand and the splitting is inverted:
$$e^4 t_2^4$$
- The lower $e$ orbital set accommodates $4$ paired electrons.
- The upper $t_2$ orbital set accommodates $4$ electrons, which split as two paired electrons and two unpaired electrons ($t_2^4$).
Thus, the number of unpaired electrons is $2.0$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] Calculate the spin-only magnetic moment (in Bohr Magnetons, rounded to two decimal places) of $[\text{Mn}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$. (Take $\sqrt{35} \approx 5.92$)
questions.solution:
In $[\text{Mn}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$:
- Manganese is in the $+2$ oxidation state: $\text{Mn}^{2+} = [\text{Ar}] 3d^5$.
- Water is a weak field ligand, forming a high-spin complex:
$$t_{2g}^3 e_g^2$$
- All five $d$-orbitals are singly occupied, so $n = 5$ unpaired electrons.
$$\mu_s = \sqrt{n(n + 2)} = \sqrt{5(5 + 2)} = \sqrt{35} \approx 5.92\text{ BM}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] If the crystal field splitting energy for an octahedral complex is $\Delta_o = 18000\text{ cm}^{-1}$, calculate the crystal field splitting energy $\Delta_t$ (in $\text{cm}^{-1}$) for the corresponding tetrahedral complex with the same metal ion and ligands.
questions.solution:
Using the relation between tetrahedral and octahedral crystal field splitting:
$$\Delta_t = \frac{4}{9}\ \Delta_o$$
Substitute $\Delta_o = 18000\text{ cm}^{-1}$:
$$\Delta_t = \frac{4}{9} \times 18000 = 4 \times 2000 = 8000.0\text{ cm}^{-1}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] Among the following coordination complexes: $[\text{Ni}(\text{CO})_4], [\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]^{4-}, [\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}, [\text{Zn}(\text{NH}_3)_4]^{2+}, [\text{Cu}(\text{NH}_3)_4]^{2+}, [\text{Fe}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$, how many are DIAMAGNETIC?
questions.solution:
Evaluate the magnetic character of each complex:
1. $[\text{Ni}(\text{CO})_4]$: $\text{Ni}^0 (3d^8 4s^2) \rightarrow 3d^{10}$ with strong $\text{CO}$, $sp^3$ tetrahedral, $n = 0 \implies$ Diamagnetic
2. $[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]^{4-}$: $\text{Fe}^{2+} (3d^6)$, low-spin $t_{2g}^6 e_g^0$, $n = 0 \implies$ Diamagnetic
3. $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$: $\text{Co}^{3+} (3d^6)$, low-spin $t_{2g}^6 e_g^0$, $n = 0 \implies$ Diamagnetic
4. $[\text{Zn}(\text{NH}_3)_4]^{2+}$: $\text{Zn}^{2+} (3d^{10})$, completely filled, $n = 0 \implies$ Diamagnetic
5. $[\text{Cu}(\text{NH}_3)_4]^{2+}$: $\text{Cu}^{2+} (3d^9)$, $n = 1 \implies$ Paramagnetic
6. $[\text{Fe}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$: $\text{Fe}^{2+} (3d^6)$, high-spin $t_{2g}^4 e_g^2$, $n = 4 \implies$ Paramagnetic
Total number of diamagnetic complexes $= 4.0$.
